newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Duke bulks up for competition.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Duke bulks up for competition.

text.p: Duke Energy Corp, to be formed by the merger of Duke Power Co and PanEnergy Corp, expects to be one of a handful of national electric retailers once barriers to competition are lifted across the country, executives said on Monday.

But the company's natural gas business will continue to operate from wellhead to the gates of its large industrial and commercial customers, initially stopping short of expanding to the doorsteps of retail customers.
"I don't think we have a strong desire to get down to the household level, right to the doorstep," Paul Anderson, PanEnergy president and chief executive officer, said in an interview with Reuters.
Duke plans to merge with PanEnergy in a $7.7 billion stock transaction, the latest chapter in the ongoing convergence of the electric and natural gas industries.

Duke President Richard Priory, who was tapped as chairman of the merged company, said the $23 billion company will have the financial strength to muscle its way into the deregulated retail electric market nationwide.
"The reality is you are going to have to be big to bring competition to the (retail) customer," Priory said.
